name: Swell
title: Swell SvelteKit Storefront — Svelte Commerce Connector
description: Svelte Commerce on Swell: 23 of 43 services wired, with cart, checkout and sign-in; reviews, wishlist, vendors and states are gaps. Setup, keys and fixes.
lede: Solid core coverage: cart, checkout and sign-in are wired against Swell’s storefront API, authenticated with the store’s public key. Reviews, wishlist, vendors and states are the recorded gaps.
verdict: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired; reviews, wishlist, vendors and states are not.

quickStart.text: one connector at a time: remove the two the storefront ships with, add this one
point it at your Swell store

quickStartNote: The guide removes only `@misiki/litekart-connector`. A fresh clone’s `package.json` also lists `@misiki/vendure-connector`, and with two connectors installed and neither of them Litekart’s, the build stops and asks for `PUBLIC_CONNECTOR` — so this removes both.

env.name: PUBLIC_SWELL_API_URL
env.note: Your storefront origin, such as `https://<store>.swell.store`. Boot fails, naming this variable, if it is missing.

env.name: PUBLIC_SWELL_API_KEY
env.note: The store’s public key, sent on its own as HTTP Basic to the storefront API.

env.name: PUBLIC_SWELL_STORE_ID
env.note: The store ID. With the secret key it authenticates Swell’s Backend API, which the connector refuses to call from a browser.

env.name: PUBLIC_SWELL_API_SECRET
env.note: The secret key, for Backend API calls. See the limitations before setting it.

env.name: PUBLIC_CONNECTOR
env.note: Only when more than one connector is installed: `@misiki/swell-connector` names the one this build runs on.

envNote: `init.ts` hands the connector every `PUBLIC_SWELL_*` variable that is set, camel-cased. The guide also lists `PUBLIC_SWELL_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `PUBLIC_SWELL_ACCESS_KEY` and `PUBLIC_SWELL_CHANNEL_ID`; the connector’s source does not read them.
backendSettings: For cash on delivery, add a manual payment method named `cod` in Swell’s payment settings; without one, the storefront’s cash-on-delivery option is refused.
Let the storefront’s origin make cross-origin requests to Swell (CORS): in production the browser calls `PUBLIC_SWELL_API_URL` directly, not only the server.
howItWorks: Swell has two APIs. The storefront API takes the public key alone as HTTP Basic, and it is the one the storefront calls. The Backend API takes the store ID and secret key, and the connector refuses to call it from a browser.

Installing the package is the whole switch. `vite.config.ts` resolves whichever `@misiki/*-connector` is installed, and `src/lib/core/connectors/init.ts` hands it every `PUBLIC_SWELL_*` variable that is set, camel-cased, at boot — in the server hook for server rendering and in the client hook for the browser, which must reach the same URL in production.

There is no Litekart API behind the storefront here, so store identity — name, logo, currency, menus, plugin toggles, theme colours — comes from `src/lib/core/connectors/default-store.json` merged under the default export of `kitcommerce.config.ts`. Until you override it, the store is called “Test”. Any Litekart REST path the connector still inherits is answered from that local data, or resolved empty, rather than requested.
limitations: Pages that depend on a service that is not wired render their empty state rather than failing.

Setting `PUBLIC_SWELL_API_SECRET` would put Swell’s secret key in every visitor’s browser: SvelteKit sends `PUBLIC_` variables to the browser, even though the connector only calls the Backend API from the server.
Homepage sections other than the live product list come from the active theme’s static content — the standing rule for themes.
The Conversational Shopping assistant is Litekart-only; its widget stays hidden when another connector is active.

troubleshooting.problem: Boot fails with “the swell connector is active but PUBLIC_SWELL_API_URL is not set”
troubleshooting.fix: Add `PUBLIC_SWELL_API_URL` to `.env`. A production Node build and Docker read `PUBLIC_*` from the process environment rather than `.env`, so set it on your deploy platform too.

troubleshooting.problem: The build stops with “Several commerce connectors are installed … Set PUBLIC_CONNECTOR to pick one”
troubleshooting.fix: More than one `@misiki/*-connector` is in `package.json` and none is Litekart’s. Uninstall the ones you do not run — a fresh clone also lists `@misiki/vendure-connector` — or set `PUBLIC_CONNECTOR='@misiki/swell-connector'`.

troubleshooting.problem: Boot fails with “PUBLIC_…_API_URL is set, but it configures a different backend than the one this build runs on”
troubleshooting.fix: Another backend’s variable is still set, usually left over from the one you switched from. Remove it, or install that backend’s connector. `PUBLIC_LITEKART_API_URL` is exempt: it only points the dev proxy.

troubleshooting.problem: The store is called “Test”, or shows the wrong name and logo
troubleshooting.fix: Store identity is static on this backend. Set `name`, `logo`, `currencyCode` and the rest in the default export of `kitcommerce.config.ts`; `src/lib/core/connectors/default-store.json` lists every field.

troubleshooting.problem: `[swell] no native implementation for get /api/...` in the console
troubleshooting.fix: The connector’s REST guard caught a path inherited from Litekart and answered it empty instead of requesting it. Each path is reported once. Harmless if Swell has no such feature; if it has one, the fix belongs in the connector’s matching service.

troubleshooting.problem: `http proxy error: api/... ECONNREFUSED` in dev
troubleshooting.fix: A Litekart REST path was requested from outside the connector, so its guard never saw it. Vite proxies `/api` to `PUBLIC_LITEKART_API_URL`, or to `localhost:7000`.

`@misiki/kitcommerce-core` declares it as a peer, and `vite.config.ts` redirects that specifier to whichever connector is installed. Make sure exactly one `@misiki/*-connector` is listed in `package.json`.

faq.q: Can I run a Swell store on Svelte Commerce today?
faq.a: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired; reviews, wishlist, vendors and states are not. Like every connector, it has not been run against a live production Swell store.

faq.q: How do I switch Svelte Commerce to Swell?
faq.a: Remove the connectors the storefront ships with, install `@misiki/swell-connector`, set `PUBLIC_SWELL_API_URL` in `.env` and start the dev server. `vite.config.ts` resolves whichever connector is installed, so no file in the storefront changes.

faq.q: Which Swell keys does the storefront need?
faq.a: The public key, for the storefront API. The secret key is for Swell’s Backend API, which the connector will not call from a browser — and because every `PUBLIC_` variable reaches the browser, it is better left unset.

faq.q: Has the Swell connector been run against a real Swell store?
faq.a: Not against a live production instance — no Svelte Commerce connector has been. It was written by reading Swell’s authoritative API source, and the Svelte Commerce maintainers ask Swell’s own maintainers for a sandbox to run it against.
